answer: I would like to talk about a holiday I took to Cox's Bazar, home to one of the longest natural sea beaches in the world. I went there last winter with a few close friends from university, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable trips of my life. We took an overnight bus from Dhaka, which was tiring, but the excitement kept us going. The beach itself was absolutely [[stunning]], stretching as far as the eye could see. We spent our days swimming, walking along the shore and watching the most spectacular sunsets I have ever seen. One morning we hired a jeep and drove along the Marine Drive towards Inani beach, with green hills on one side and the sea on the other, which was unforgettable. We also stopped at Himchari, where a small waterfall runs down the hillside, although it was only a trickle in the dry season. In the evenings we sampled fresh seafood, which was [[delectable]], especially the grilled fish from the little stalls near the beach. What made it special was the combination of natural beauty and good company, which is a hard thing to beat. We laughed constantly and stayed up late talking, just like in our student days. Being by the sea was genuinely [[rejuvenating]] after months of office life. Honestly, there is something about the vastness of the ocean that puts your everyday worries [[into perspective]]. I came home feeling completely recharged, and it left me with [[cherished]] memories that I still look back on fondly.

followUps.q: Would you go back to Cox's Bazar?
followUps.answer: Yes, without a doubt. Next time I would like to take my parents, because my mother has never seen the sea properly, and I think watching the sunset there together would be very special.

followUps.q: Do you prefer holidays with friends or with family?
followUps.answer: Both have their charms. With friends, trips are more spontaneous and adventurous, while family holidays are calmer and more comfortable. At my age, I probably enjoy the energy of travelling with friends slightly more.
